c.tagline: Where the Great Wall meets the sea and Beijing goes to the beach.

taxi.fareNote: Metered from about ¥8; summer beach-season demand in Beidaihe can mean waits and negotiated flat rates. Pay by Alipay/WeChat or cash.

emergency.note: 110 reaches police, 120 an ambulance, and 119 the fire service; there is no single combined emergency number, and 112 works from mobiles to route you.

hood_landmark.Gold Coast (Beidaihe New District): Gold Coast sand dunes, Changli, Qinhuangdao

avoid.reason: Expect vendor overcharging and tout pressure at Beidaihe and Nandaihe beaches in summer; agree on prices first.

hood_desc: Qinhuangdao's downtown port district and its economic and administrative core, with the main railway station, shopping streets, and the Olympic Sports Center; the practical, year-round base with the best transport links.

China's most famous seaside summer resort, a leafy district of sandy beaches, sanatoriums, and villas that fills with holidaymakers from Beijing and Tianjin each summer; the place to stay for the beach and Pigeon Nest Park sunrise views.

The walled Ming garrison town where the Great Wall meets the sea, home to the 'First Pass Under Heaven' gate and Old Dragon's Head (Laolongtou); Qinhuangdao's headline history and its most sightseeing-rich quarter.
A quieter beach-resort strip just south of Beidaihe with wide sands, water parks, and the Nandaihe International Entertainment Center; a calmer, family-friendly alternative to busy Beidaihe.

The Gold Coast (Huangjin Hai'an) dunes and Beidaihe New District to the south, known for China's tallest coastal sand dunes, birdwatching wetlands, and newer resorts; a spread-out, nature-focused area.
lodging: Home Inn Qinhuangdao Beidaihe New District

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water, as everywhere in mainland China.

transit.hours: City buses run roughly 5:30 AM to 9:30 PM, with extra tourist lines in the summer season; there is no metro.
transit.note: Qinhuangdao has no metro; city buses link the port district (Haigang) with the Beidaihe beaches and Shanhaiguan, supplemented by taxis, DiDi, and seasonal tourist shuttles in summer.
transit.pay: Pay by scanning an Alipay or WeChat Pay QR code, tapping a rechargeable transit card, or cash (exact change, flat ¥1-2 fare) on board.

bus: Coaches to Beidaihe, Shanhaiguan, and across Hebei

car.idp: Not valid — China does not recognize the International Driving Permit; a temporary Chinese driving permit is required to drive.

ferry: Qinhuangdao Port and seasonal passenger boats on the Bohai Sea
train: Qinhuangdao Railway Station and Beidaihe Station (Beijing–Harbin and Beijing–Shenyang high-speed rail)

transit.m: Airport shuttle bus to Beidaihe / Qinhuangdao downtown (~40 min)
Taxi to the city center (20-30 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary or expected in China; no service charge or gratuity is needed at restaurants, hotels, or taxis.
